items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that 'no root repeats across the gap' between 23:22 and the 23:24-25 couplet is byte-false.
items.evidence: 23:22's own father/mother tokens recur two verses later: לְ֭אָבִיךָ and אִמֶּֽךָ at oshb:Prov.23.22 reappear as the byte-identical forms אָבִ֥יךָ and וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ opening oshb:Prov.23.25, with the construct אֲבִ֣י also opening oshb:Prov.23.24 -- three tokens of the shared pair span exactly the gap the row says carries none. This does not by itself overturn the single-verse call -- 23:23 still opens a distinct topic and shares no root with either neighbor, and a shared theme alone would be over-clustering -- but the row's own stated ground for rejecting the cluster alternative is factually wrong.

items.claim: The claim that 23:23 shares 'no vocabulary' with its neighbors is imprecise: it shares a root with 23:24's wisdom/wise pairing, though not the exact wordform.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.23.23's חָכְמָ֖ה ('wisdom') and oshb:Prov.23.24's חָ֝כָ֗ם ('wise') are cognate forms of the same root -- an unqualified negative that a root-level check would have caught. The root recurs across dozens of Prov verses book-wide, so this does not disturb the single_proverb call -- 23:23 still lacks a motive clause and shares no exact wordform with either neighbor -- but the absolute 'no vocabulary' phrasing overstates the case.

items.claim: 23:29 carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note sitting inside the verse quoted as the row's central 'six-fold' rhetorical evidence, and the verse-31 form the row calls 'the span's one plain imperative' is grammatically a negated prohibitive, not a true imperative.
items.evidence: The marks inventory records one ketiv/qere note at 23:29 that the row never mentions despite quoting Hebrew directly from that verse and resting its rhetorical-structure argument on it; the pair sits inline inside the verse's third 'who has' clause, the unpointed ketiv מדונים immediately followed by the pointed qere מִדְיָנִ֨ים -- exactly the inline-ketiv pattern that is easy to miss when slicing a K/Q verse. Separately, oshb:Prov.23.31's אַל תֵּ֥רֶא is negative-particle-plus-prefix-conjugation (a prohibitive/vetitive construction) -- Hebrew's true imperative mood has no negated form -- so calling it 'the span's one plain imperative' mislabels the form; argued from the pointed bytes since morphological tagging is not machine-checkable here.
